elicitation_input.question: where are mucosal associated lymphoid tissues present in the human body and why

llm_generation.text:
Mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue (MALT) is present beneath mucosal surfaces throughout the body, especially in the gastrointestinal tract—including the small intestine, appendix, and tonsils—as well as the oral and nasopharyngeal passages, lungs, thyroid, breast, salivary glands, eyes, and skin.  

It is located there because mucosal surfaces are major points of contact with food, microbes, and airborne particles. MALT provides a first line of immune defense by sampling antigens, producing immune responses, and maintaining tolerance to harmless food and commensal organisms.
